findings.title: Expired cache rows are reported as active cache
findings.body: This query includes cache rows regardless of `expiresAt`, but availability lookup only serves rows whose `expiresAt` is still in the future. Since expired rows remain in the table, the UI can show a cache status and offer deletion when no usable cached data exists. Filter the status query to unexpired rows, or otherwise distinguish expired data.

findings.title: Legacy cache rows are assigned a false last-updated timestamp
findings.body: Adding `updatedAt` with `DEFAULT NOW()` assigns the migration time to every existing cache row, even though those rows may have been created much earlier or may already be expired. The status UI then presents this migration time as the cache's last update. Backfill from a timestamp that reflects the original cache write (for example, `expiresAt` minus the cache TTL), or avoid presenting the migration default as historical update data.

findings.title: Deleting cache leaves the connected-calendars status stale
findings.body: The delete mutation does not invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`; it only invokes an optional `onSuccess` callback, which may be unset or may not refetch this query. After a successful deletion, the cached `cacheUpdatedAt` remains in the UI, so the status and delete action continue to indicate that cache exists until some unrelated refetch occurs.

findings.title: The environment-file update uses BSD-only sed syntax
findings.body: `sed -i ''` is the macOS/BSD form of in-place editing and fails with GNU sed, so running this helper on typical Linux development environments will not update `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` in the environment file. Use a portable in-place edit or handle GNU and BSD sed separately.
